questionSequence.question: When did this policy last change?
What does byteMyCache itself store in my browser?
What do embedded services store, and when?
How do I clear or block it?

argumentMap.belief: A returning reader can see when the policy last changed.
The reader knows byteMyCache sets no cookies of its own and stores one thing, their light/dark choice in local storage, and that analytics stores nothing on their device.

The reader knows outside storage appears only when they use something: the YouTube player after they press play, Amazon after they follow an affiliate link, and Cloudflare's spam check on the contact form once they start filling it in (named only if Task 11 Step 6 finds it stores anything).
The reader knows their browser settings clear or block all of it, that blocking storage only resets the theme to the default, and where to ask.

contract.maximalHonestPromise: A visitor can see every item byteMyCache and its embeds store in their browser, why, and how to clear or block it.
contract.signedThesis: byteMyCache sets no cookies of its own and stores only your light/dark choice, analytics stores nothing on your device, and embedded services add their own cookies only when you use them.

deliberateOmissions.reason: Readers who open a cookies page know; padding.
The site has none and needs none under option A; describing one would be false.

deliberateOmissions.section: Per-vendor cookie names for YouTube, Amazon, Cloudflare Turnstile
deliberateOmissions.reason: Unverified and changed by those vendors; their policies are the authority.

lensReview.rationale: It dates the policy for a returning reader.
It names the single item and settles the analytics question, the page's core answer.
It tells the reader exactly when outside cookies appear, which they can then avoid.
It gives the reader the controls that actually work and the contact route.
